title: T1573 — Encrypted Channel
subtitle: The animation replays one full encrypted C2 session: TCP connect, TLS handshake, key exchange, symmetric beaconing, tasking, and the two SOC views that catch it - metadata...

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.tip: Sensitive data - What is at risk

steps.title: The implant opens a TCP connection
steps.caption: Malware on the victim PC starts and connects to the C2 server on TCP port 443. The enterprise firewall sees a brand-new outbound flow to an IP address it has never seen before and writes it into its connection log
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: The TLS handshake happens
steps.caption: The implant sends a TLS ClientHello, and the C2 answers with a ServerHello plus a self-signed certificate. The connection content is still readable at this point, and the handshake details are now stored in the Zeek ssl.log file
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Keys are exchanged (asymmetric step)
steps.caption: The two sides run an ephemeral Diffie-Hellman agreement - the Zeek log shows curve x25519 - and derive the session key. Older TLS 1.2 setups instead wrapped a session key with the server's RSA public key. From the network view either way, this is just more bytes inside the handshake
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: The encrypted beacon starts
steps.caption: Both sides switch to a fast symmetric cipher, and the implant sends its first beacon: a small encrypted blob about every 60 seconds. Nobody in the middle can read it, but its regular shape is visible
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Tasking and results
steps.caption: The C2 pushes a task to the implant, for example a command to run. The implant executes it and returns the output through the same encrypted channel, which shows up as bidirectional bursts inside long-lived TLS flows
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: SOC view one: metadata
steps.caption: The SOC analyst checks the metadata: the JA3 fingerprint is rare in this environment, the certificate is self-signed, and the server name (SNI) does not match the certificate common name. Each signal alone is weak; together they are strong
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

detection.label: Partial signal
detection.detail: A weak signal exists but is not yet a confirmed alert.

steps.title: SOC view two: timing
steps.caption: The SOC checks timing statistics: a connection every 60 seconds, sizes in a narrow band around 250 bytes, and long session durations. This beacon pattern is detectable even though the traffic can never be decrypted
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

detection.label: Alert raised
detection.detail: The SOC has enough evidence to open an incident.

steps.title: Block and hunt
steps.caption: The SOC blocks the rare JA3 fingerprint at the egress firewall and sends the C2 domain to a sinkhole (a DNS service that returns a safe, blocked address), then hunts across all hosts for the same fingerprint and certificate to scope the intrusion. The victim PC is isolated for cleanup
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.
